note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is, and it is empty for a reason: no South Dakota party page that a program may read publishes an endorsement for a November 3, 2026 state or local race. South Dakota's parties choose their candidates by primary (Governor, the Legislature, county offices) and by state convention (Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, Auditor, Treasurer, Commissioner of School and Public Lands, Public Utilities Commissioner); those are nominations, already shown as the party label on the ballot, and the parties' pages list their nominees without the word endorsed (or supported, or recommended). Such bare lists are recorded neither as endorsements nor as other support: they add nothing to the label. No party page read names a candidate for a nonpartisan contest (city council, conservation, water or power district) or an independent. Three parties have candidates on the November list (Republican, Democratic, Libertarian); 'Independent' is not a party. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first (none forbade it): the three state parties' sites and every county or district unit's own website linked from the Republican and Democratic directories (home page plus candidate, election and news pages, ten pages a site at most; each searched for the word, and the listing pages opened a second time and searched again). Web search was not available for this run, so a unit whose website is not in its state party's directory was not found; guessed addresses for the larger Republican county units did not exist. Facebook and other social media pages were not read. Federal offices are outside this file.
